Bill.BriefDescription: Establishing requirements for a less restrictive alternative for persons committed as sexually violent predators.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to less restrictive alternatives; and amending RCW71.09.092.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 71.09.092 and 1995 c 216 s 10 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Before the court may enter an order directing the conditionalrelease of a person committed under this chapter to a less restrictivealternative, it must find the following: (((1))) (a) The person will be treated by a treatment provider who isqualified to provide such treatment in the state of Washington underchapter 18.155 RCW; (((2))) (b) The treatment provider has presented a specific course oftreatment and has agreed to assume responsibility for such treatmentand will report progress to the court on a regular basis, and willreport violations immediately to the court, the prosecutor, thesupervising community corrections officer, and the superintendent ofthe special commitment center; (((3))) (c) Housing exists that is sufficiently secure to protect thecommunity, and the person or agency providing housing to the p. 1 SSB 6399conditionally released person has agreed in writing to accept theperson, to provide the level of security required by the court, andimmediately to report to the court, the prosecutor, the supervisingcommunity corrections officer, and the superintendent of the specialcommitment center if the person leaves the housing to which he or shehas been assigned without authorization; (((4))) (d) The person is willing to comply with the treatment provider andall requirements imposed by the treatment provider and by the court;and (((5))) (e) The person is willing to comply with supervision requirementsimposed by the department of corrections. (2) In approving a treatment provider as provided in subsection (1)of this section, the court shall give due deference to the providerrecommended by the department.
